title: Intentional Invisibilization in Modern Asian History: Concealing and Self-Concealed Agents
summary: Concealing Agents addresses the invisibilization and concealment of people, knowledge and ideas in history and historiography. With studies ranging from modern to contemporary history, language and translation studies, and digital archival sciences, this book provides an interdisciplinary perspective to better understand how people become absent and marginalized, through the lens of bondage and dependency in Asia.
